text: The Bill also aims to support economic opportunities in innovative circular business models and the rising demand for resource recovery in Singapore and the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It is critical that we manage our e-waste properly: first, to avoid contaminating our landfill and water catchment with toxic substances; second, to protect the health of workers who handle these discarded products; and third, to extract valuable materials that can be recycled into new products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will do so through the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework, which makes producers financially and physically responsible for the end-of-life collection and treatment of their products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have no plans to bring the start date forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Industry feedback has highlighted that both producers and recyclers need sufficient time to adjust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The framework will apply to electrical and electronic equipment, or what we call "triple E" (EEE), which are categorised as Information and Communications Technology (ICT) equipment, batteries, lamps, solar panels and large appliances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Large appliances will now include electric mobility devices like e-scooters and power-assisted bicycles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Arising from industry feedback, NEA will appoint a single Producer Responsibility Organisation (PRO) to reap economies of scale.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Producers of EEE for the consumer market, such as laptops and mobile phones, will be required to finance the PRO.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will exempt small producers from financing the PRO to avoid imposing disproportionately high costs on them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: PRO will collect and send the e-waste for recycling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: All producers of non-consumer EEE will be required to take back all end-of-life products for free upon request.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This covers commercial and industrial equipment, such as solar panels and data servers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will not require them to finance a PRO, as they have existing take-back processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Retailers must also offer free one-to-one takeback services during delivery; for example, to take away the old refrigerator when delivering a new one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Further, retailers with an EEE sales area of more than 300 square metres must provide in-store collection points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This provides consumers with convenient avenues for recycling e-waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Many retailers and partners already provide such collection points voluntarily.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, NEA partnered StarHub, DHL and TES to bring the RENEW programme to Best Denki, Courts, Gain City and Harvey Norman.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: They have collected more than 3,200 kilogrammes (kg) of e-waste across 20 outlets since June last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Altogether, there are currently about 500 e-waste recycling bins island-wide, which can be located via myENV app.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I encourage everyone to take advantage of these convenient channels to recycle your e-waste, including rechargeable lithium-ion batteries from our mobile phones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Chairman, with your permission, I would like to show some slides.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We note Mr Louis Ng's suggestion on the recovery of coltan.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are still consulting the industry on the recycling requirements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To support this framework, NEA will actively develop the e-waste industry, such as the skills and capabilities of our local recyclers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will create more good job opportunities for Singaporeans, including opportunities in the PRO, supply chain management and e-waste recycling.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Packaging waste, including plastics, is another priority for my Ministry.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Louis Ng asked for more details on the mandatory packaging reporting framework for businesses to be introduced in 2020.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will require producers of packaging and packaged products to report to NEA how much packaging they put-to-market annually.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They must also submit their plans to reduce, reuse or recycle packaging waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA will monitor the companies’ packaging data and 3R plans over the next few years and explore with them ways to reduce packaging waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA will also engage companies to simplify reporting procedures and minimise compliance costs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Similar to e-waste, we are studying how producers can assume responsibility in collecting and treating packaging waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: An EPR framework would incentivise upstream reductions in packaging, an outcome similar to what Mr Louis Ng envisaged through setting mandatory reduction targets.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: EPR is a more holistic way of addressing packaging waste, including single-use plastics.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, by voluntarily changing the packaging design and optimising production practices, Nestlé Singapore has saved 2,000 tonnes of packaging used for its MILO® products.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is not only good for the environment; it also reduces business costs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to engage the 3P sector as we develop this EPR framework.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Even as we study EPR, we are working with the industry on new initiatives to collect back packaging waste, such as PET bottles and aluminium cans.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, we are collaborating with partners to tap on the Towards Zero Waste Grant to roll out 50 reverse vending machines in major malls and the community later this year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh suggested a need to address packaging due to the rise in online shopping and home delivery.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Supermarkets, which usually offer online retail services and home deliveries, will be covered under the mandatory packaging reporting requirements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked about the current state of food waste and our measures to manage this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In 2018, we generated 763,000 tonnes of food waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We conducted a food waste segregation pilot at Tampines Greenlace estate in August last year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The residents participated actively, with one in three households depositing food waste in dedicated bins at least once a week.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Over three months, more than 4,000 kg of food waste from Tampines Greenlace were recycled into fertilisers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The residents were delighted to receive packets of the fertiliser, a very tangible symbol of their efforts in closing the food waste loop.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The pilot, which was due to end in October last year, has been extended at the request of the residents.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are encouraged by their enthusiasm and are working with Zero Waste SG to explore how we can enhance involvement and ownership by the community.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I am also glad that with the support of NEA's 3R Fund, onsite food waste treatment systems have been installed in 23 premises.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are now ready to expand food waste segregation, starting with larger food waste generators.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA has started consulting the industry on requirements for food waste segregation for treatment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Premises include hotels and malls, and industrial developments housing food manufacturers, caterers and food storage warehouses.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Existing premises can choose the treatment solution that best suits their operations, including offsite treatment at the upcoming Tuas Nexus.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Unlike existing premises, new premises can plan for onsite food waste treatment in their building design.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will require developers of new developments where large amounts of food waste are expected to be generated to cater for onsite food waste treatment to be implemented.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These must be included in the building plans submitted from 2021.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to provide support for premises and invite interested parties to implement onsite food waste treatment before the mandatory requirements take effect.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Premises can tap on funding support, such as the 3R Fund.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: My Ministry will also work with owners of large public sector buildings with F&B outlets to segregate food waste for treatment from 2021.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are exploring doing so under the Public Sector Taking the Lead in Environmental Sustainability (PSTLES) initiative.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: PSTLES already builds environmental sustainability into our Government procurement, which Mr Louis Ng asked about.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Public sector agencies must purchase Energy Star-certified ICT equipment, eco-labelled printing paper and energy-efficient appliances.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked if we proactively identify companies with greater potential to reduce waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This focuses attention on waste generation by premises and the potential for reduction and recycling.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: More than 90% of hotels and malls covered have now adopted recycling programmes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These are factories, warehouses and convention and exhibition centres above a certain gross floor area.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah also spoke about the dilemma of replacing disposables with reusables which require washing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA's lifecycle assessment on the environmental impact of carrier bags and food containers showed that reusables had a lower overall environmental impact than disposables.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, opting for reusables is better for the environment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the use of disposables for dining-in at hawker centres, which is already disallowed in new hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA will continue to work with existing stallholders to not use disposables for dine-in.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked about promoting the reuse of construction and demolition (C&D) waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, waste concrete is mostly processed to produce recycled aggregates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is a good example of the circular economy in action!

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: BCA has published a Sustainable Construction Guide with useful information on recycled construction materials and their applications.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ms Irene Quay raised the issue of medication waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I agree it is important to curb over-prescription of medicine.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: By not over-buying medication that will be wasted, patients also save money.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Some hospitals limit prescriptions to no more than three months’ supply of normal medicine and no more than six months’ supply for chronic illnesses.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Certain pharmacies put additional labelling on drug packaging to inform patients to return unused drugs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Pharmacists also counsel patients and review their medication supply to ensure that patients do not take more medication than needed.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Generally, household drugs can be safely disposed of together with household waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All our household waste is collected and safely incinerated before the ash is landfilled in Semakau Landfill.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Some people may not know this, but my Ministry also oversees the planning of after-death facilities and services, which some may view as a morbid endeavour.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And, indeed, it is – pardon the pun – a deadly serious matter that has to be handled sensitively.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Low Thia Khiang asked for an update on the provision of the Inland Ash Scattering (IAS) facilities and the proposed post-death rites facility at Tanah Merah.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA is working on the designs to incorporate suggestions from consultations with funeral service providers, religious leaders and members of the public.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When completed, these secular facilities will be an additional option for bereaved families to lay their loved ones to rest in a dignified and respectful environment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Environmental Impact Study commissioned for the proposed post-death rites facility at Tanah Merah is in progress.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will consider the results of the study and public feedback before arriving at a final decision.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked about actions taken against the contractor who had provided quartz instead of marble plaques when relocating niches from Mount Vernon Columbarium Complex.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There was no evidence from NEA’s investigation to suggest that the contractor had deliberately provided a different material with the intention to cheat.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA’s checks also showed that the marble and quartz plaque prices were comparable.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA has required the contractor to remedy the breach of contractual requirements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As a further penalty, the contractor will also bear additional manpower costs incurred by NEA to oversee the niche replacement works.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA will continue to monitor the replacement works closely.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So far, there have been no anomalies detected during laboratory tests and visual inspections.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I will now move on to hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our hawker centres serve important social objectives of providing affordable food in a hygienic environment for patrons, enabling hawkers to earn a decent livelihood and creating vibrant social spaces to bond our communities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, hawkers face many challenges today, from changing demographics and customer preferences to new models of competition, such as central kitchens and food delivery services.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It can be even more difficult for hawkers in new hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They face competition from other F&B options in the vicinity and need time to build up their clientele.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is why my Ministry piloted the SEHC model to help hawkers compete better as a Centre.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As Mr Liang Eng Hwa said, last year, NEA addressed concerns on contractual terms, such as opening hours and termination notice periods.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I visited all seven SEHCs to get feedback from the stallholders on the changes made and am pleased that the majority of stallholders have welcomed them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to improve the model based on feedback from hawkers and other stakeholders.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: One area of concern is attracting and supporting new entrants into the hawker trade.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Without new hawkers, future generations would not be able to enjoy hawker food.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is, therefore, critical that we imbue new hawkers with key skills to succeed.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is why NEA set up the Incubation Stall Programme (ISP) and worked with the People's Association and ITE to set up hawker training programmes that cover business management and operation, marketing and culinary skills.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are also enhancing the ISP based on the experience and feedback from our incubation stallholders.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is to address feedback that more time is needed to establish their business.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are also piloting the extension of NEA's ISP to SEHCs which can provide guidance to hawkers under the ISP.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This leverages their experience and success in supporting hawkers under their own incubation stall programmes, including the provision of mentors for the hawkers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: One new hawker joining NEA's ISP is Mr Jim Yeow, who will operate his incubation stall – Mr Louis Ng may be pleased to know – at Yishun Park Hawker Centre, an SEHC, and receive mentorship support from its operator, Timbre.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I have tasted his wanton noodles, which are quite exceptional.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, please do try it when the stall opens.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, I have gone around to meet many young aspiring hawkers and am inspired by their entrepreneurship, passion and resilience.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Many offer their own brand of tasty hawker food.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, I urge Members of this House and all Singaporeans to support them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Today, I had specially arranged for Cheng Tng from XX Dessert and Min Jiang Kueh or pancakes with fillings like Thai Milk Tea and Belgian chocolate besides the classic peanut filling from Munchi Delights to be served at the Members Room.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Both stalls are located at Yishun Park Hawker Centre.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In particular, XX Dessert is run by Yishun Park Hawker Centre's youngest hawker, 23-year-old Mr Peh Zixuan.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: He started out under Timbre's incubation stall programme after completing his National Service.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, you could say he truly turned from "Ah Boy to Man".

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I hope Members will have a chance to enjoy these during the teabreak.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I heard that the Min Jiang Kueh literally flew off the trays!

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In November last year, I had a dialogue with some members of the Hawker Centre 3.0 Committee and other stakeholders, including hawkers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It was suggested that we set up ground-up workgroups to look at issues related to the hawker trade and culture.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are, therefore, facilitating the formation of two workgroups – one to explore ideas to attract and support new entrants to the hawker trade, and another to look at encouraging graciousness and tray return, issues that were also raised by Mr Gan Thiam Poh.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The two workgroups will comprise hawkers, food advocates and members from various fields.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As part of our productivity efforts, we want to encourage existing hawker centres to adopt measures, such as automated tray return stations integrated with centralised dish washing (CDW) services.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At Block 163 Bukit Merah Central, hawkers and cleaners enjoy a reduced workload and a 40% reduction in water bills due to the productivity measures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Currently, stallholders at existing hawker centres receive two years of subsidies under the Productive Hawker Centre Grant to ease the transition to such productivity measures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These will help hawkers realise manpower and cost savings in the longer term.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Stallholders have raised concerns about the increase to the full costs of CDW at the end of two years.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It will be co-located with the MND-MOH assisted living residential flats pilot in Bukit Batok Town bounded by Bukit Batok West Avenues 6 and 9 and Bukit Batok Street 41.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When completed, this new hawker centre will provide an affordable food option to residents in the area.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We welcome the newly-minted Singapore Food Agency (SFA) to the MEWR family come April and look forward to working with the agri-food industry to help forge a great future for the industry from farm-to-fork.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked what we will do to ensure market-friendly regulations without compromising on food safety.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These two objectives are mutually-reinforcing, as food safety is key to developing a thriving agri-food industry.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The industry has been supportive of the formation of SFA and has given feedback on how SFA can partner them to support both objectives.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: One suggestion was the harmonising of licensing standards and streamlining licensing conditions for food businesses along the food value chain.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, we are looking at how premises carrying out both central kitchen and catering operations can obtain a single licence instead of two.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: A better understanding of the emerging challenges facing it will allow us to identify opportunities for collaboration among stakeholders.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There are also opportunities in areas, such as digitalisation of food tracing using block chain technologies, and innovations in the production of new foods.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Chairman, there is an African proverb: "If you want to go fast, go alone.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If you want to go far, go together." Realising the ambitions of our Zero Waste Master Plan to build a sustainable Singapore will require strong partnerships to co-create and implement new solutions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I will conclude with a call to action in two areas for the Year Towards Zero Waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, I urge everyone to participate in the public consultations for the Zero Waste Master Plan which Mr Louis Ng and Miss Cheng Li Hui asked about.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These will form the final phase of our ongoing consultations on the Master Plan.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Last month, I also met more than 20 green groups.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Many are driven by young and passionate environmentalists, such as those from Ground-Up Initiative and Foodscape Collective, who have been championing for the environment and promoting sustainable living.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They see the urgency of changing mindsets and rallying everyone to do his or her part for the environment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Many of these are eco-champions and they are brimming with ideas and keen to work together to achieve our vision of a Zero Waste Nation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Even what I am wearing today is a product of our eco-champions' passion and innovation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This dress is created by The Fashion Pulpit for the Fashion 3R initiative, which promotes sustainable fashion.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is upcycled from two different second-hand dresses to give them a brand-new lease of life.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Second, in conjunction with the #RecycleRight Movement, I invite interested individuals and organisations to partner us to better educate Singaporeans and others, including domestic helpers, on recycling properly.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is not merely about consulting or conducting focus group discussions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We want to co-create effective recycling solutions together.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, let us start our journey of co-creation to reduce the contamination of our recycling bins, including possibly co-creating legislation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Chairman, as Minister Masagos Zulkifli said earlier, "We are not done building a sustainable Singapore".

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will need everyone to play their part, to conserve our resources, embrace the 3Rs and adopt a circular economy approach so that we can continue to build a sustainable Singapore for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have some time for clarifications but no more photographs of food because it is near dinner time.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Can the Minister elaborate more on this, and will it affect our drinking water supply and water security?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Indeed, we are not privy to what is happening to the company because the company is, of course, exposed to many other factors that may affect its performance.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I have a clarification for Senior Minister of State Amy Khor.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I think she mentioned that the Public Service does do some procurement which are very environmentally sustainable.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But could I ask whether we can specifically include this into the procurement principles, not just based on fairness, transparency and value-for-money, but put it in writing that it should also be based on environmental sustainability?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The second clarification is on whether we can provide incentives or subsidies to the hawkers so that they will not use disposables for dine-ins.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I know we are not using it in our new hawker centres and new stalls in old hawker centres.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But can we just move it to all hawker centres and maybe provide some incentives to nudge the behavioural change?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, under PSTLES, they are already practising procurement taking into account environmental sustainability.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, that is why procuring energy-efficient appliances, equipment, sustainability sourced paper, are all part of PSTLES.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Government procurement principles will be general and the procurement principles are really about transparency, that you need to tender out and so on and so forth.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But for environmental sustainability, the public sector has already taken the lead by drafting these guidelines on procuring and taking the lead in terms of environmental sustainability, not just in procurement, but also in other areas.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to the question about incentivising hawkers to use disposables, we do not have any intention to do that at this present moment, but what we have done is to look at encouraging the existing hawkers to not use disposables for dine-ins.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In the case of hawker centres that are already on our Productive Hawker Centres programme, which means they use centralised dishwashing and tray return, they already will not be allowed to use disposables for dine-in.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What we are hoping to do now is to work with the Hawkers Association and with the ground to encourage the hawkers to try and get them onto the Productivity Hawker Centre programme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That really is to encourage more to come on board.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Those that come on board will then not use disposables for dine-in.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we are looking at how we can encourage more to come on board.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I have three clarifications for the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: First, is the Tanah Merah facility for sea burial confirmed to be built?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Or does it depend on the outcome of the environmental impact studies?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: The second clarification is on the two Inland Ash Scattering sites.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Can I take it that they are confirmed to be built?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Or are they again waiting for some studies?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Lastly, I understand that the Ministry has been in the design phase of the two sites.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I asked the same question since last year.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: How long more will it take for the design and consultation to be completed?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: And when can the public expect some information or more information on the sites?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to the Tanah Merah site for the post-death rites facilities, as I have noted, the environmental impact studies are still in progress.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Once the study is completed, NEA will consider the findings, taking into account the public feedback and suggestions as well.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will also look at the concerns of parents, the water sportsmen, as well as some members of the public.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we will take all these into account before coming to a decision on the proposed post-death rites facilities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That is why I said that they are on track.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The facilities will be completed by 2020 and 2021, but we are still in the design and planning stage because we have already undertaken the consultation and we are taking this on board in the design of the facilities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, once they are ready, we will share with the public.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: I have two clarifications for Senior Minister of State Amy Khor.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: The first is: when she shared about the disposal of drugs, that they can be safely disposed and trashed, can I confirm if she was referring to all drugs, including cytotoxics and antibiotics?

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: I understand that NEA does have guidelines on the special handling of drugs, such as cytotoxics and antibiotics.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: My second concern, as mentioned in my speech, is not just about safe disposal, but it is also about the risk of accidental ingestion as well as diversion for illicit use.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: So, would NEA be keen to still explore take-back programmes?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding recycling, we will need to work with MOH on this, because, obviously, there are issues of safety and so on with regard to the drugs, for instance, once they are opened, are there issues and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, this is something that NEA will have to work closely with MOH.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Reports have said that if the defaults are not managed properly and the restructuring is going to fail, Hyflux is going to basically close shop.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: If that happens, would it affect the other operations of Hyflux in Singspring Desalination Plant, Bedok NEWater and Jurong Membrane Bioreactor Plant?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Would it affect the operations there and would that, therefore, affect the water supply?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: The second clarification is: does this whole episode regarding Tuaspring say something about the viability of public-private partnership in areas that are existential to us?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Would the Government reconsider its position to make sure that these things do not happen anymore?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Just like TPL, PUB has been onsite, in all the plants, we have been monitoring, we always monitor.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We look at the operational readiness of these plants and then we also see whether they can keep up to the capacities that they are designed for and if they should default, the same step-in rights can be invoked.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But more importantly, this 3P model, the large part of our water system is under PUB.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, this is not a huge part of what we have.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In adopting the 3P model, we get many advantages, we are able to not invest in capital, pay only for what we need.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We also can build the local capabilities of our enterprises, who can also then bring these for export purposes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the same time, we also know there are risks involved and, therefore, we have put in enough measures to be able to take over the plant or own it in the event that these 3P partners are not viable anymore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And this is exactly what we are doing now where TPL is concerned.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Is there a timeline for zero emissions for the public vehicle fleet?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: We heard a bit about MOT's plans for the bus fleet, but there are other large public vehicle fleets – Police vehicles, Civil Defence and so on.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: So, perhaps, would the Ministry have any plans they can elaborate on for this?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When we took steps to reduce the number of diesel vehicles, it is really to enhance and increase the quality of our air.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And this is not just through the diesel tax that we increased recently.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have the Vehicular Emissions Scheme under the Certificate of Entitlement scheme where we incentivise or disincentivise the use of pollutive or non-pollutive vehicles.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We also have the Early Turnover Scheme which encourages diesel owners or companies to turn over their old vehicles into new vehicles.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And this is important because heavy goods vehicles under the Euro VI standard are 20 times cleaner than the older ones or the oldest ones that are under the Euro I standards.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the same time, it is also more fuel-efficient.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It shows that all these three measures are taking effect.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: More importantly, the sum of all these, including the decrease of the number of diesel vehicles on the road, from these classes of vehicles, have actually contributed to the decreasing trend of Particulate Matter (PM) 2.5, which is very important.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The World Health Organization's (WHO's) Advisory tells us that PM2.5 is carcinogenic, it can cause cancer.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The tightened industrial emission, together with these, have seen the contribution of PM2.5 reducing over the years.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But the bad news is, we are still above the WHO standards and, therefore, we still have to do more.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Can we do away totally with diesel vehicles?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But for the moment, let us do this slowly, and help the industry transform and, at the same time, make sure that all of us breathe clean air.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is really an omnibus of various legislation that, if you put together, we could call it a Climate Change Bill, in the absence of which, it is sufficient now, for what we have.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, would you like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Chairman, we are all very proud of our Water Story.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I am sure all of us are looking forward to another success story – that is, our food story.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: And I would like to thank my Government Parliamentary Committee members for speaking up so passionately.
